gaps.title: Rename is not shown in the capture
gaps.description: DEC-001 defines managing documents as upload, rename, delete and share. The captured Documents screen shows Upload, Share and Delete controls but no rename control, flow or state. How a document is renamed, who may rename it, and what rules apply to names (for example duplicates or file extensions) are not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Rename is one of the four confirmed management capabilities for this document library, and the mockup gives no basis for specifying it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: One of four confirmed capabilities is specified without any designed interaction, or it is left out.

gaps.title: Who may upload, rename, share and delete is undefined
gaps.description: The roles question (CQ-002) was answered with text that only lists capabilities (DEC-002) and names no roles. DEC-004 and DEC-005 introduce an owner and shared recipients with viewer or editor rights, but which of upload, rename, share and delete each of owner, editor and viewer may perform is not stated. 'Editor' rights are also undefined, because editing document content is not in the confirmed scope of managing (DEC-001). The Document entity shows no owner or sharing information, and the row's Share and Delete buttons are shown with no indication of who sees them.
gaps.why_it_matters: Security is defined as only people the owner shares with can open a document, so every action on a document depends on knowing what an owner, an editor and a viewer may do.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Editors or viewers could delete, rename or reshare documents the owner did not intend, breaking the confirmed security rule; or legitimate users are blocked.

gaps.title: Share flow, revocation and recipient experience not shown
gaps.description: Share has no captured destination. DEC-005 states owners share with named colleagues as viewer or editor, but how a colleague is identified or found, whether access can be changed or revoked, what a recipient sees (including whether shared documents appear in their Documents list and how they differ from owned ones), and what happens to someone who has a document open when access is revoked are not shown in the capture and not answered.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing is the only way access is granted under the confirmed security definition, so its flow determines who can open each document.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Access cannot be withdrawn or audited by owners, or recipients cannot find shared documents, undermining both the sharing and the security requirement.
research_questions: How do widely used document tools (for example Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive/SharePoint, Dropbox) let an owner share with named people as viewer or editor, change that role and revoke access?
How do these tools show documents shared with a user separately from documents the user owns?
What happens in these tools when access is revoked while the recipient has the document open?

gaps.title: Delete confirmation, recoverability and effect on shares not shown
gaps.description: Delete (trash icon) has no captured destination. Whether a confirmation is shown, whether deletion is permanent or recoverable, whether it can be undone, and what happens to existing shares and to recipients' access when an owner deletes a shared document are not shown in the capture and not answered.
gaps.why_it_matters: Delete is a confirmed capability shown as a one-click icon on each row, and a deleted document may also have been shared with colleagues who depend on it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Documents can be lost irreversibly by a mis-click, and recipients may lose access without warning.
research_questions: What confirmation and recovery patterns (confirmation dialog, undo window, trash with retention period) do common document-management tools use for deleting files?
How do common document tools handle shared recipients' access when the owner deletes a shared file?

gaps.title: Upload flow and its rules not shown
gaps.description: Upload has no captured destination. What a click opens, allowed file types and maximum sizes, whether several files can be uploaded at once, what happens on upload failure, and how a duplicate file name is handled are not shown in the capture and not answered.
gaps.why_it_matters: Upload is the only observed way documents enter the library, and the confirmed library size of up to 1,000 documents depends on its limits.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Upload behaviour, limits and failure handling are decided ad hoc during build, and duplicate names may overwrite or confuse documents.
research_questions: How do common document tools handle uploading a file whose name already exists in the folder (rename, replace, keep both)?
What feedback patterns do common tools use for multi-file upload progress and per-file failure?

gaps.title: Library behaviour at up to 1,000 documents is undefined
gaps.description: REQ-005 requires pages to load within two seconds for a library of up to 1,000 documents. The capture shows one row only; whether the list is searchable, sortable, filterable or paginated, its default order, and which pages and conditions the two-second target is measured on are not shown or stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: A 1,000-document list is both the performance target and what users must navigate to manage documents 'easily'.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The performance requirement cannot be tested consistently and users may be unable to find documents in a large library.
research_questions: How is page load time conventionally measured for a web page (for example Core Web Vitals such as Largest Contentful Paint) and what conditions are used?
What list patterns (pagination, infinite scroll, search, sort) do document tools use for libraries of around 1,000 items?

gaps.title: Empty, loading, success and error states not shown
gaps.description: Only one state with a single document row is captured. The empty library, loading, success feedback after upload, rename, share or delete, and failure states for each action are not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: A new user starts with an empty library, and every confirmed action can fail; 'easily' manageable depends on clear feedback.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users get no feedback or misleading feedback, and states are designed inconsistently during build.
research_questions: What established guidance exists for empty, loading and error states in file-list interfaces?

gaps.title: Unlabeled icon actions may lack accessible names
gaps.description: Delete is a trash icon in an actions column the inventory records as unlabeled. Whether row actions have accessible names that identify the document, keyboard operability and focus handling after a row is deleted are not shown.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-003 label 'unlabeled actions column', action 'Delete (trash icon)'

gaps.why_it_matters: Each row repeats Share and Delete; without document-specific names, screen-reader users cannot tell which document an action affects, which is especially risky for Delete.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users of assistive technology may delete or share the wrong document; the feature may not meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 success criteria apply to icon-only buttons repeated in table rows (for example 1.1.1, 2.4.6, 4.1.2), and what do they require?
What does WCAG 2.2 require for focus management after an item is removed from a list (for example 2.4.3)?

gaps.title: Colleague accounts and ownership lifecycle undefined
gaps.description: Sharing targets 'named colleagues' (DEC-005), but which population counts as colleagues, whether sign-in is required, and what happens to a document and its shares when its owner or a recipient leaves or their account is deleted are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Because only the owner can grant access, an owner's departure could leave documents nobody can manage or reshare.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Documents may become orphaned, or former colleagues may keep access, contradicting the confirmed security rule.

gaps.title: Notification of recipients when shared or revoked undefined
gaps.description: Whether a colleague is told when a document is shared with them, when their role changes or when access is revoked, and through which channel, is not stated and not shown.
gaps.why_it_matters: Named-colleague sharing only works if recipients learn a document is available to them.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Recipients may not find shared documents, or notifications are added without agreed content or channel.

gaps.title: Traceability of sharing and deletion undefined
gaps.description: Whether share, role change, revocation, rename and delete actions must be recorded (who, what, when) is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Security is defined by who the owner shared with; without a record, it cannot be established who had access to a document or who deleted it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Access disputes or accidental deletions cannot be investigated.

gaps.title: 'Modified' format, meaning and time zone undefined
gaps.description: The Modified column shows a relative value ('2 days ago'). The format for older dates, the time zone used, and whether it reflects uploads, renames or sharing changes are not shown or stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Modified is the only date users see to identify recent documents; its meaning changes depending on whether rename or sharing updates it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users misread document recency, and sorting by date may be inconsistent.
research_questions: What conventions do common file managers use for switching from relative to absolute timestamps, and which events update a file's modified date?

assumptions.text: DEC-002's verbatim answer ('Managing means upload, rename, delete and share.') does not answer which roles manage documents or how 'easily' is judged, so CQ-002 is treated as still open.
assumptions.why: The recorded answer matches CQ-001, not CQ-002.
assumptions.impact: Roles and permissions are raised as a critical customer gap (GAP-002).
assumptions.to_confirm: Which users or roles manage documents and what acceptance measure applies to 'easily'.

assumptions.text: The captured Documents screen (SCR-001) is the library page that the two-second load target in REQ-005 applies to.
assumptions.impact: GAP-006 ties the performance target to the documents list.
assumptions.to_confirm: Which pages and operations the two-second target covers.

assumptions.text: 'Named colleagues' means users within the same organisation who have accounts in the product.
assumptions.impact: GAP-009 treats account lifecycle as relevant to sharing.
assumptions.to_confirm: Who can be selected as a share recipient.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Roles allowed to manage documents are unanswered (DEC-002 did not address CQ-002), and rename is not shown in the capture.
Revocation, role changes, recipient experience and what editor rights allow are not stated.
Which actions owners, editors and viewers may perform is not stated.
